event: Natalie brings the hot dish out and asks Amy to pass her a towel.
Third try at the bread: the first loaf was a brick, the second a sponge, this one bread.
Amy says it smells incredible and cuts into it, rested or not.
Natalie: bread doesn't rest, steak does; bread is eaten while the butter has an opinion.
Zadi calls that the best thing said at the table all year, Middlemarch night included.
Amy: Zadi argued Middlemarch alone till one; Amy fell asleep on the couch.
Zadi says she was very persuasive, and calls the bread a whole event.
It's Natalie's grandmother's recipe, from the little tin box with the rooster on it.
Half the cards are lists with no instructions: flour, buttermilk, the good honey, patience.
It took her three loaves to learn what patience meant in her grandmother's hand.
Amy guesses the oven was slower in her grandmother's day.
Exactly: an extra quarter hour at a lower heat, and her grandmother was there.
Zadi finished the Robin McKinley she'd carried around for two weeks like a small pet.
"The dragon one?" "The dragon one."
She won't spoil the ending, but closed the book and just sat holding it.
It landed like a full cup set down without a ripple; she read the last page twice.
Amy notes two weeks is fast for Zadi with a book she likes; she usually rations them.
Zadi failed to ration it, has no regrets, and now gets to choose the next one.
She has three on the shelf making their cases.
Natalie: let them audition and bring something to the table.
The salad tomatoes are hers, she says: the first real bowlful off those vines.
Amy recognises the ones Natalie nursed along in June like they were in intensive care.
They turned the corner in the sunny bed by the fence, talked to scandalous.
Zadi says the salad tastes like July did its job.
Amy spent Sunday in the pantry with the radio on; the nicest afternoon in weeks.
Everything's in jars now; she opened the door this morning just to look at it.
Natalie: that's the best feeling, shelves you can trust.
Amy found three cans of the same beans behind everything: hence the bean salad.
Zadi: a dish with a backstory always tastes better.
Natalie: every good table is nothing but backstories, like the recipe box.
Cobbler's coming: peaches from the county-road stand with the dog that supervises the till.
Amy: the dog that sits on the stool like an employee? Natalie: like middle management.
She bought two baskets, and the dog approved the transaction personally.
Zadi wants him written into a small, honest novel where the peaches are always ripe.
Natalie says tonight's chapter is in the oven; y'all save room.
Amy saved room, planned in advance with contingencies.
Zadi: she means she skipped lunch. Amy: she had a strategic lunch.
The cobbler comes out, its crust pretty; Natalie sends for the cream in the blue pitcher.
Zadi asks everyone to stop talking for a second: this deserves quiet.
They eat in quiet; Natalie credits the dog-supervised county-road peaches.
Zadi likes this part best: candles low, nobody in a hurry, the talk taking its shoes off.
Amy: the week can sit down somewhere; it's off duty.
Natalie: you cook dinner so the evening has somewhere soft to land.
Zadi: next month is her table; she cooks soup well, and will buy the bread.

memory.fact: Natalie, Amy and Zadi share a supper once a month, and take turns hosting it.

event: There will be a short traditional poem before anyone is allowed to leave.
Natalie wouldn't miss it, and will bring the good honey for the bread.
Amy will bring labels in case Zadi's pantry wants to become trustworthy.
Zadi: her pantry is beyond help, but Amy may try. Is there more decaf?
Natalie: the pot's still warm; sit, hosting means she gets to say that.
Amy notes the candles are almost down to the wood; she likes them like this.
Zadi: everything's gone all amber.
Natalie: that's the hour, the best light of the day, nothing to do but sit in it.
Natalie pours more cream for Amy: now they're all where they're supposed to be.
